name: google/agents-cli

hlido_opinion.headline: Official Google tooling that makes any coding assistant better at scaffolding, evaluating and deploying ADK agents on Google Cloud — a force multiplier, not an agent itself.
hlido_opinion.body: This is a first-party Google project (under the `google` GitHub org, documented on the Google Developers Blog), and it's important to be clear about what it is: agents-cli is a CLI plus a skills package for building, evaluating and deploying AI agents on Google Cloud — the agents themselves are built with Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK), and agents-cli handles everything around them: scaffolding, evaluation, deployment, and observability. It's explicitly a tool for coding agents, designed to make Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity or any other assistant fluent in the ADK-on-Google-Cloud lifecycle — while also working standalone from your terminal (`agents-cli scaffold/eval/deploy`). The strategic read is that Google is doing what platform owners do: reducing friction from create to production so its Agent Platform becomes the path of least resistance. The credit here is real — first-party maintenance, a coherent create-to-production story, and local development possible with just an AI Studio API key. The honest limits: value is tightly coupled to Google Cloud and ADK, so it's a lock-in-adjacent choice; there's no pricing on the tool surface because the cost lives in the cloud resources it deploys; and as a young first-party tool the independent evidence of real-world reliability is still thin.

tier_rationale: STEADY (80) because it's genuinely useful first-party infrastructure with a clear, coherent purpose (the ADK-agent create-to-production lifecycle) and the trust that comes with official Google maintenance. Not VITAL because it is deliberately ecosystem-bound (ADK + Google Cloud), which is a real portability trade-off, and because it's early enough that independent reliability evidence beyond Google's own docs is limited.
what_it_does_well: Official Google tool — first-party maintenance and documentation via the Agent Platform
Coherent create-to-production lifecycle: scaffold, evaluate, deploy, observe
Works both as a skill layer for coding assistants AND standalone from the terminal
Local development possible with just an AI Studio API key (no immediate Cloud spend to try)
Composes with multiple assistants (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, etc.)
what_it_fails_at: Tightly coupled to Google's ADK and Google Cloud — portability/lock-in trade-off
No standalone value for teams not building on ADK
Cost is opaque at the tool level because it lives in the Cloud resources deployed
Young project — independent reliability evidence beyond Google's own docs is thin
best_for: Teams building agents with Google's ADK who want a paved deploy path
Developers using a coding assistant who want it fluent in ADK-on-Google-Cloud
Anyone standardising agent scaffolding, eval and observability on Google Cloud
not_recommended_for: Teams committed to a non-Google stack or avoiding cloud lock-in
Projects not using the Agent Development Kit
Buyers wanting a portable, vendor-neutral agent framework

compared_to.verdict_diff: AutoGen is a vendor-neutral multi-agent framework you assemble yourself; agents-cli is Google's opinionated lifecycle tooling around its own ADK. Choose agents-cli for a paved Google-Cloud deploy path, AutoGen for framework portability.

CrewAI is a build-anywhere agent-orchestration framework; agents-cli is not a framework at all but the scaffold/eval/deploy tooling around ADK. They sit at different layers — pair agents-cli with ADK if you're on Google Cloud, use CrewAI if you want stack independence.

evidence_urls.claim: Official Google project: CLI + skills for ADK agents on Google Cloud
Scaffold, evaluate, deploy, observe lifecycle; works standalone or with coding assistants
Covered by Google Developers Blog (Agent Platform)
Local dev with AI Studio API key; requires Python 3.11+, uv, Node.js

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: High for the ADK-on-Google-Cloud niche. It is itself agent-infrastructure: a CLI + skills that coding agents consume to scaffold/eval/deploy other agents. Value is conditional on building with Google's ADK.
